1920: You finished the snack, turned the empty bag inside out for more, and found only the memory of it.
1921: The coffee cooled from hot to merely warm in the time it took to find somewhere to set it down.
1922: They poured your drink, and the ice took up most of the cup, leaving a thoughtful trickle underneath.
1923: You unwrapped the meal one tiny lid at a time, a small ceremony for a very modest banquet.
1924: The snack was described as a biscuit. It was, technically. It was also mostly air and good intentions.
1925: You got a napkin before the drink arrived, and you sat holding it, fully prepared, for a long while.
1926: The bag warned it may contain traces of nuts. It contained, in the end, exactly three.
1927: Your tea came with a bag, a cup, and hot water that had opinions about staying hot. It did not stay hot.
1928: You accepted a second snack when offered, then quietly hid it away for the emergency you were sure was coming.
1929: The main dish was warm in the middle and cool at the edges, a careful little map of someone's effort.
1930: You ordered the drink you never touch at home, on the logic that nobody up here knew you well enough to judge.
1931: The tray table folded down at exactly the wrong angle for a tall person, and today you were a tall person.
1932: The cart blocked the aisle just as you needed to stand, so you sat back down and ordered a snack instead.
1933: You got one cookie, wrapped like it was precious, and honestly, at that height, it was.
1934: The coffee came black because you forgot to ask, and you drank it that way with dignity you did not feel.
1935: The tiny pretzels were gone in three bites, and you spent the next hour thinking fondly about them.
1936: You unfolded the little napkin and it turned out larger than the entire meal it was meant to accompany.
1937: The cart offered you everything, and after long thought you chose the one you always choose. Water.
1938: You bit the mystery snack, chewed slowly, and decided it was fine, which is a whole review, really.
1939: The creamer cup was smaller than your thumb, and you emptied all of it in for the smallest bit of comfort.
1940: They gave you a warm towel before the meal, and unsure what to do, you thanked it very sincerely.
1941: The meal came with a plastic packet you could not open and eventually admired for its dedication.
1942: You took the last snack of its kind, and the cart rolled on carrying nothing but apologies for the rest of the plane.
1943: The soup, if it was soup, stayed warm exactly as long as it took to unwrap the spoon. Then it didn't.
1944: You raised the tiny cup in a quiet toast to no one, because a drink at altitude deserves a moment.
1945: The bag had a picture of a pretzel bigger than any pretzel actually inside it. Bold advertising, honestly.
1946: The tray had a little well for the cup, and sliding your drink into it felt like solving a small puzzle.
1947: Your snack and your neighbor's snack were identical, and you both eyed each other's anyway, just checking.
1948: The coffee refill never came, so you nursed the last cold inch of it as if it might refill itself.
1949: You finished the meal and stacked every tiny empty container back on the tray, feeling oddly accomplished.
1950: The clouds looked solid enough to walk on, and part of you seriously considered the offer.
1951: Down below the whole world shrank to a thing you could hold in one hand, and you felt briefly, absurdly in charge.
1952: You pressed your face to the cold glass and left a small foggy print of your own nose. Art.
1953: The roads below curled like dropped string, and you solemnly traced one to its end, achieving nothing at all.
1954: From up here the cars crawled along like patient little beetles, all very sure of where they were going.
1955: The sun came up over the wing so slowly it felt like it was doing it just for you. It wasn't.
1956: A wall of cloud slid across the window and held the whole view hostage for a while. You waited it out.
1957: The fields down there were stitched into neat little squares, as if someone had tidied the whole planet.
1958: You watched your own plane's tiny shadow race across the clouds far below and quietly cheered for it.
1959: The window was cold enough to keep a drink against, and for a long while you seriously considered doing that.
